questions.question: Which of the following is the full form of ASCII?

options.text: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Scientific Code for Information Interchange
Asian Standard Code for Information Interchange
Analytical Standard Code for Intermitted Information

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ASCII stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange.**__
 
• It's a standard data-transmission code used by smaller and less powerful computers to represent textual data (letters, numbers, and punctuation marks) as well as non-input-device commands (control characters).
 
• Like other coding systems, it turns data into **standardised digital formats** that let computers communicate with one another and process and store data more efficiently.
 
• The ASCII code was created for teletypewriters but has now found widespread use in personal computers.
 
• Seven-digit binary integers, or numbers made up of multiple sequences of** 0s and 1s**, are used in the standard ASCII coding.
 
• Because there are 128 different possible combinations of seven 0s and 1s, the code can represent **128 different characters.**
 
• A lowercase "p" is represented by the binary sequence 1110000, while an uppercase "P" is represented by the binary sequence 1010000.
 
• The seven information bits plus a **parity bit **(used for error-checking purposes or to represent special symbols) in ASCII code are usually placed in an eight-bit field.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique identifier for each user, typically in the format of name@domain.com?
questions.solution:

__
 
• An **email address** is a unique identifier for each user, typically in the format of **name@domain.com**.
 
• Email addresses are used to **send and receive electronic messages** over the internet.
 
• They consist of two main parts: the **local part** (before the @ symbol) and the **domain part** (after the @ symbol).
 
• The domain part usually represents the email service provider, such as **gmail.com** or **yahoo.com**.
 
• Each email address must be **unique** to ensure that messages are delivered to the correct recipient.

• The local part of an email address can include **letters, numbers, and certain special characters** such as periods, underscores, and hyphens.
 
• It is case-insensitive, meaning **user@example.com** and **User@Example.com** are considered the same.
 
 
 
• **Domain Part**
 
 
• The domain part follows the @ symbol and typically represents the email service provider's domain name.
 
• Common domains include **gmail.com**, **yahoo.com**, and **outlook.com**.
 
• It can also include custom domains, such as **yourcompany.com**.
 
 
 
• **Email Protocols**
 
 
• **SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol)** is used to send emails.
 
• **IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol)** and **POP3 (Post Office Protocol)** are used to retrieve emails from a server.
 
 
 
• **Email Clients**

questions.question: What do you mean by LAN?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Local Area Network**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Local Area Network (LAN)** is a network that connects computers within a limited area such as a residence, school, laboratory, university campus or office building.
 
• LANs are characterized by higher data-transfer rates, smaller geographic range, and lack of a need for leased telecommunication lines.
 
• They are typically used to share resources such as files, printers, games, or other applications.
 
• LANs can be wired (using Ethernet cables) or wireless (using Wi-Fi).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wide Area Network (WAN)**

 
 
• A WAN spans a large geographic area such as a state, province, or country.
 
• WANs often connect multiple smaller networks, such as LANs or MANs.
 
• The most well-known example of a WAN is the Internet.
 
• WANs are typically established using leased telecommunication lines.
 
 
 
• **Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)**
 
 
• A MAN spans a larger area than a LAN but smaller than a WAN, such as a city or a large campus.
 
• MANs are designed to extend over an entire city, and they may be used to connect several LANs within a city.
 
• MANs are typically owned by a single organization such as a government entity or large corporation.
 
 
 
• **Personal Area Network (PAN)**
 
 
• A PAN is a computer network organized around an individual person within a single building.
 
• PANs are used to connect personal devices such as computers, smartphones, tablets, printers, and other devices.
 
• Bluetooth and USB are common technologies used to create PANs.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is used while printing documents in MS

Word 365, i.e. if we want to print all the pages from 7 till 10, then the printer should print only the 7th, 8th, 9th and 10th pages?

__
 
• **Print Custom Range:**

 
 
• This setting allows you to specify the exact pages you want to print within your document.
 
• Instead of printing the entire document, you can select a specific range of pages.
 
• For example, to print pages 7 through 10, you would enter "7-10" in the "Pages" field of the Print dialog box.
 
• This is useful when you only need specific sections or portions of your document.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This option is particularly useful when printing on single sheets of paper or if your printer doesn't support double-sided printing.
 
 
 
• **Collated:**
 
 
• When printing multiple copies of a document, the "Collated" option arranges the pages in the correct order for each copy.
 
• For example, if you're printing two copies of a four-page document, collated printing will produce two sets of pages 1-4, rather than printing all copies of page 1, then all copies of page 2, and so on.
 
 
 
• **Orientation:**
 
 
• This setting determines the page layout:
 
• Portrait: The page is taller than it is wide (the standard orientation for most documents).
